notes: SHIP v1.14.433 - M2-b STAGE 1: THE DATA CONTRACT (RACKENGINE-SPEC section 7, invariants I8 and I9). Callers pass a rackId. The engine resolves. WHAT WAS WRONG. Six call sites each did their own racksByCab[id] lookup and handed a rack OBJECT to master_rackToElevation - and master_renderHit handed a hand-made { hosts: ... } instead of the record. Two shapes for one concept with nothing forcing them to agree: the reshape divergence section 7 exists to end. RackEngine._resolve(rackId) now returns { id, label, units, devices, source, dataState } and every device carries u, height, type, label, hostname and status. IT WRAPS THE CANONICAL SHAPER, IT DOES NOT REPLACE IT. master_rackToElevation owns U extraction, height-unknown stamping and the totalU floor, and re-implementing any of that here would be exactly the second-door mistake v1.14.431 cost a ship to learn. What _resolve ADDS is the three things section 7 asks for that the shaper cannot know: the LOOKUP so callers pass an id and never an object (I8), type NORMALISATION through Vocabulary before any renderer sees it (I9), and SOURCE plus DATASTATE so an empty rack says which kind of empty it is (R-06). Pinned by test: the resolver calls master_rackToElevation and does NOT contain master_extractRu or master_nodeHeightInfo. NORMALISING IN THE RESOLVER IS ONLY SAFE BECAUSE Vocabulary.typeOf IS IDEMPOTENT. The flat writer already normalises since .429, so a value passing through both is unchanged - pinned three levels deep for all eleven codes in spec 20, and re-pinned here as a resolver invariant. Without that guarantee this would double-map and silently downgrade real gear to unknown, which is the failure mode the .246 blank-panel incident is a written record of. R-06 IS NOW REPRESENTABLE. An EMPTY rack and an UNKNOWN rack are different answers: a cab the Master holds with no devices resolves source master and dataState empty, while a cab the Master has never heard of resolves source standalone and dataState unassigned. Collapsing those two into one nothing-here is what made an honest empty cabinet read as corruption twice, once triggering an ordered production rollback. A zero-component rack is a valid rack state, not a missing-rack state. ONE SILENT-FAILURE SHAPE CLOSED WHILE ROUTING. Callers consume _resolve(id).elevation directly, and the first draft returned no elevation at all for an unknown cab - handing a renderer undefined, which is precisely the class Contract 14 forbids. elevation is now ALWAYS an object on every path, including empty and null ids, and that is pinned. ROUTED, DELIBERATELY NARROWLY: the two Command-hero lookups, which were literally racksByCab[id] plus id, and master_renderHit, which was the reshape. Both hit builders were checked first and return the FULL record host array with the racksByCab key as id, so the swap is semantically identical and only removes the reshape - verified before changing it rather than assumed. SCOPE HELD. attach, the reclaim barrier (I6), modes and the section 8 deletions are NOT in this ship. Section 8 ends by deleting forge3d_render as a separate renderer, in the subsystem that cost eight ships to stabilise and where .427 fixed a live defect two versions ago. That is not a same-ship change. TESTS: new spec 22-data-contract, eight tests - the contract shape, no RAW code surviving, double-normalisation being a no-op, empty versus unknown as distinct answers, elevation never undefined on any path including null, the reshape gone from master_renderHit, the resolver wrapping rather than re-implementing, and the routed hero path still producing slots and a totalU floor. 22 plus 09 plus 20 plus 02: 33 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. No UI surface changed, no CSS changed. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: none required - this is a data-path refactor with no visual change, and the routed surfaces are covered by 09 and 02.
